transcript.text: Hi everyone. I wanted to get us together to review the public operating plan for Signal Garden before we publish visitor information. As you know, I'll be making the final approval decision, but I need to walk through the plan with rights and licensing and accessibility first as part of our normal process. The draft proposes walk-up admission, six daily sessions, a capacity of 60 people per session, and recording by the festival for promotional use. I'd like to hear from both of you on your respective areas before I sign off.

transcript.text: I reviewed the signed artist license this morning and there are three key constraints we need to address. First, Signal Garden may only be presented as ticketed sessions — so the walk-up admission proposal isn't permitted under the license. Second, the festival may not record the installation, so the promotional recording plan would violate the agreement. Third, all visitor materials must use the exact credit wording 'Signal Garden by Nia Okafor.' These are all hard requirements from the artist's license, so the draft plan will need to be revised before we can publish visitor information.

transcript.text: I completed an on-site accessibility assessment this week, and there are three key findings that affect the operating plan. First, the installation can accommodate at most 40 people per session — not the 60 in the draft. Second, it requires exactly four daily sessions rather than the six proposed. And third, we need a 15-minute room reset between sessions for mobility equipment and sensory-access preparation. These are hard accessibility requirements that will need to be reflected in the revised plan.
